questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

I tried to tell him to think of the good times, that __every cloud has a silver lining__.

options.text: Doing something with thoroughness and passion
Don’t cry over what has happened as it cannot be fixed
Treat people the same way as you want to be treated
Every difficult situation has a hopeful aspect to it

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Every difficult situation has a hopeful aspect to it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate meaning of the given idiom 'every cloud has a silver lining' is 'Every difficult situation has a hopeful aspect to it'.
 
• Every cloud has a silver lining: even a very bad situation has a positive or hopeful side.
 
 
• *Example: He told us about his resignation—an absolute disaster at the time, but **every cloud has a silver lining **because it led to my appointment.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 4.​

 

Correct Sentence:__ *Every difficult situation has a hopeful aspect to it.*

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

His successful as a lawyer / grew so fast that he soon had / enough money to buy a house.

options.text: grew so fast that he soon had
enough money to buy a house

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'His successful as a lawyer.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in 'His successful as a lawyer' of the sentence.
 
• The word '**successful**' means '**having achieved** what you wanted; having become popular, rich, etc.'
 
 
• *Example: It was a successful tournament for Team India.*
 
 
 
• Whereas the word '**success**' means '**the fact** that you have achieved what you want.'
 
 
• *​Example: Hard work is the key to success.​*
 
 
 
• Therefore, the use of 'successful' in the sentence should be replaced with 'success' to make it grammatically correct.

 

Correct sentence__: *His __**success**__ as a lawyer grew so fast that he soon had enough money to buy a house.*

questions.question:

My sister called me for my lunch hours to tell me that she was getting married.

questions.solution:

• The error lies in 'My sister called me for__ my' of the sentence.
 
• We use '__**for'**__ to talk about a purpose or a reason for something.
 
• The **correct word** to use in place of '**for**' is '**during**'.
 __
 
• *Example: I’m going for some breakfast. I’m really hungry.*
 
 
 
• 
 **During** means within the period of time mentioned.

 
 
•

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Consumers are not ready to purchase this citrus fruit at such a ______ price.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is-'high'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's check each option:
 
 
• higher: It is the **comparative** degree of the word 'high'. It is used during comparisons.

 
 
• Example- He loved to climb hills, the higher the better.
 
 
 
• highest: It is the **superlative** degree of the word 'high'. It refers to 'being at a point or level higher than all others'.
 
 
• ​Example- You have the highest marks in the class.
 
 
 
• highly: very, to a large degree, or **at a high level**
 
 
• Example- The statement was made by a highly placed official.
 
 
 
• high: **being a large distance** from top to bottom (especially of things that are not living) 
 
 
• Example- The garden is surrounded by a high wall.
 
 
 
 
 
• Hence, the most appropriate option to fill in the blank is 'high'.
 
• Thus, *option 4 *is the correct answer.

 

The correct sentence is:* **Consumers are not ready to purchase this citrus fruit at such a **high*__* price.*

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is The.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2 is The.
 
• "The" is a definite article it is used for **when we discuss a certain topic or an issue that has previously been raised in the conversation.**
 
• Thus the correct answer is **The.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• There are two types of articles** definite** and** Indefinite** article.
 
• The article is indefinite (a/an) and the article is definite (the).
 
• **When discussing something for the first time or something vague**, we utilise the **indefinite article.**
 
• **When referring to something specific or something that has already been discussed in the dialogue**, we utilise the **definite article**.
